method: Receptor-model source attribution by chemical mass balance (CMB): 8 daily Copernicus CAMS tracers, scaled by their 90th percentiles, are split by non-negative least squares into 6 fixed reference source profiles written from emission chemistry (traffic NO2+NO+CO, industry/coal SO2+NO2+CO, burning CO+HCHO, secondary O3+HCHO, dust, sea salt). PM2.5 mass yields come in two stages: a non-negative regression of CAMS PM2.5 on the source activations using within-site day-to-day variation (R2 0.57), then a calibration to observed PM2.5 at 96 reference monitors (observed = 0.87 x modelled + 7.8 ug/m3); the constant is the regional background & other. Fitted on 13243 site-days (2024-09-27 to 2025-02-28). It explains 17% of the variance of observed daily PM2.5 (11% for unseen locations); 2 of 5 pre-stated plausibility checks pass. Shares are indicative: the CAMS tracers are ~40 km grid averages with emission inventories behind them.

factors.label: Traffic & urban combustion
factors.description: Nitrogen oxides (NO2 and freshly emitted NO) with some carbon monoxide: the signature of vehicle exhaust and other street-level fuel burning, including the secondary nitrate that forms from it.

factors.label: Industry, coal & power
factors.description: Sulphur dioxide with some NO2 and carbon monoxide: the signature of coal, oil, power plants and industry, including the secondary sulphate that forms from it.

factors.label: Fires & biomass burning
factors.description: Carbon monoxide and formaldehyde with little NO2: smoke from crop, forest and savanna fires and household wood and dung burning.

factors.label: Desert dust
factors.description: Mineral dust blown from deserts and dry land such as the Sahara, Arabia and the Thar, often carried hundreds of kilometres.

factors.label: Photochemical & secondary
factors.description: Ozone with some formaldehyde: chemically aged air in which sunlight turns gases into secondary organic and inorganic particles, a regional haze found almost everywhere.

factors.label: Sea salt (marine)
factors.description: Sea-salt spray from breaking ocean waves, carried inland by onshore winds at coastal sites.

pm_regression.cv_scheme: GroupKFold(5) by 1-degree location; both stages refitted per fold

direct_obs_nnls.note: alternative: one NNLS of observed PM2.5 on the same activations

checks.name: Traffic factor is higher on working days
checks.detail: Median over 90 sites of mean weekday / mean weekend traffic activation (local weekends: Fri-Sat in the Gulf states, Iraq, Egypt, Algeria and Bangladesh, Sat in Nepal, Sat-Sun elsewhere); 45/90 sites above 1. The raw CAMS NO2 input has a median ratio of 0.990 on the same days, i.e. the global model itself shows almost no weekly cycle.

checks.name: Sea-salt share is higher at coastal than inland sites
checks.detail: Mean marine share at 29 clearly coastal sites 0.032 vs 38 clearly inland sites 0.001. The marine factor activation itself is 0.858 at the coast vs 0.017 inland; its PM2.5 coefficient is 1.02 ug/m3 per unit activation.

checks.name: Desert-dust share is highest in the Middle East, North Africa and Sahel
checks.detail: Mean dust share by region (Sahel = N'Djamena, Dakar): Middle East & North Africa + Sahel 0.211, Sub-Saharan Africa 0.072, Central Asia & Caucasus 0.025, Latin America & Caribbean 0.024, South Asia 0.015, East Asia 0.005, Europe 0.005, North America 0.003, Southeast Asia 0.000. Top sites: N'Djamena 0.470, Jeddah 0.414, Kuwait City 0.402, Abuja 0.398, Doha 0.277.

checks.name: Burning factor peaks in the Oct-Nov crop-residue season (Delhi, Lahore)
checks.detail: Mean burning activation Oct-Nov 2024 / Dec 2024-Feb 2025: New Delhi 1.12, Lahore 0.72 (value = the lower ratio).

checks.name: Factor activations explain observed PM2.5
checks.detail: In-sample R2 of the attributed PM2.5 (sum of the 6 source contributions + background) against observed daily PM2.5 over 13243 site-days at 96 monitors; out-of-fold R2 with location-grouped 5-fold CV (both stages refitted) 0.111; raw CAMS PM2.5 alone reaches R2 0.460 on the same rows. Gas tracers on a ~40 km grid carry less information than CAMS's own PM2.5 field.

examples.name: Dakar, Oct-Feb (coastal Sahel; CAMS tracers only)
